post.summary: Log in with email and password
post.description: Returns access/refresh tokens directly, or a short-lived MFA challengeToken if the account has MFA enabled (see POST /auth/mfa/verify).

post.summary: Complete login with an MFA code
post.description: Second step after POST /auth/login for an MFA-enabled account. Exchanges the login response's challengeToken plus a TOTP code for real access/refresh tokens; optionally marks this device as trusted for future logins.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new access token
Revoke a refresh token
post.description: Logs the current device out by invalidating the given refresh token. Does not affect the caller's other active sessions/devices.

post.summary: Create or update the password policy for an entity, or the global default
post.description: entityId is optional — omitted, this upserts the GLOBAL policy (entityId=null). Only the global policy is actually resolved at login/change-password time in this release; a per-entity policy can be created here but AuthService has no entity context at authentication time to apply it yet.

get.summary: List every password policy, global and per-entity

post.summary: Change your own password
post.description: Requires the current password. The new one is checked against the effective (global) policy's own complexity rules and against your last historyCount password hashes for reuse, both enforced server-side, not just advisory.

get.summary: Get your own login history
get.description: The 50 most recent events, newest first.

get.summary: Get any user's login history
get.description: The 50 most recent events, newest first.

get.summary: Get recent login history platform-wide
get.description: emailAttempted and eventType are both optional filters. The 100 most recent matching events, newest first. Unlike the two routes above, this also surfaces failed attempts against emails matching no user at all.

post.summary: Manually unlock a locked account
post.description: Ahead of the lock's own automatic expiry. Clears failedLoginAttempts to 0 and notifies the affected user.

post.summary: Begin MFA (TOTP) enrollment
post.description: Generates a secret and a QR code but does NOT enable MFA yet — mfaEnabled only flips on once POST mfa/enroll/confirm proves you can generate a valid code from it, so scanning the QR into the wrong app can't lock you out. Rejected with a 409 if MFA is already enabled.

post.summary: Confirm MFA enrollment with a live authenticator code
post.description: Flips mfaEnabled on and returns ten recovery codes in plaintext — the only time they are ever visible; only their hashes are stored. Rejected with a 401 on an invalid code, a 400 if no enrollment is in progress, a 409 if MFA is already enabled.

post.summary: Disable MFA on your own account
post.description: Requires a valid live TOTP or unused recovery code, not just your bearer token — the same "re-prove factor" principle changePassword uses currentPassword for, so a stolen access token alone can't turn MFA off. Deletes every recovery code as a side effect.

post.summary: Regenerate your recovery codes
post.description: Requires a valid live TOTP or unused recovery code, same re-authentication requirement as MFA disable. Every unused existing code is invalidated; ten new ones are returned in plaintext, the only time they are visible.

get.summary: List your own active sessions
get.description: There is no separate Session model — this lists your own non-revoked, non-expired RefreshToken rows, newest-used first.

delete.summary: Revoke one of your own sessions
delete.description: Rejected with a 403 if the session id belongs to someone else — cannot be used to probe or revoke another user's session.

post.summary: Log out every other active session — "log out everywhere else"
post.description: currentRefreshToken identifies your own in-flight session so it survives this call; every other active session is revoked.

get.summary: List any user's active sessions

post.summary: Force-logout every active session for a user
post.description: E.g. a compromised account. Unlike the self-service "revoke others" route, there is no session preserved — every one is revoked.

get.summary: List your own trusted devices

delete.summary: Revoke one of your own trusted devices
delete.description: Also revokes any still-active session that was issued via this device, so removing trust can't leave a live session standing on it. Rejected with a 403 if the device belongs to someone else.

patch.summary: Rename one of your own trusted devices
patch.description: Cosmetic only — does not affect the device's own trust or any live session.

get.summary: List any user's trusted devices

delete.summary: Force-revoke a device on a user's behalf
delete.description: E.g. reported lost or compromised. No ownership check needed (that's the self-service route's job) — still revokes any live session issued through the device.

post.summary: Create an IP allowlist rule
post.description: scope=GLOBAL applies to every user; scope=USER requires userId and applies to that user only. cidr must be a valid IPv4 CIDR — IPv6 is not supported yet. Fail-open-until-configured: a user with zero applicable active rules is unrestricted; once at least one GLOBAL or matching USER rule exists, their request IP must match one of them.

get.summary: List IP allowlist rules
get.description: scope and userId are both optional filters.

delete.description: A soft delete (isActive=false) — the row itself is kept, not removed.

get.summary: Get the account-lockout security overview widget
get.description: sinceHours (default 24) sets the trailing window for the failedLogins/lockoutEvents counts; currentlyLocked is always a live, right-now count regardless of the window.

get.summary: List my own notifications
get.description: Optional status/channel/unreadOnly filters, newest first. take is capped at 100 regardless of what is requested (defaults to 25).

get.summary: Get my own unread notification count
Get system-wide notification delivery stats (admin)
get.description: Counts by status and by channel across every user's notifications — an operational view for spotting a stuck queue or a spike in FAILED deliveries, not a way to read any individual's notification content.

patch.summary: Mark one of my own notifications read
patch.description: Rejected (403) if the notification does not belong to the caller. Idempotent — marking an already-read notification read again just returns it unchanged, not an error.

post.summary: Mark every one of my own unread notifications read
post.description: A single bulk update; returns how many were marked.

post.summary: Create an email template
post.description: code must be unique across every template.

get.summary: List email templates
get.description: isActive is an optional filter; omitted, every template is returned regardless of active state.

get.summary: Get a template by its own code

patch.description: Every update bumps the template's own version by 1 — there is no separate history table, version is the only trace of prior edits.

post.summary: Render a template against sample data without sending anything
post.description: No Notification row is created and no email is sent — a pure render, for an admin to check a template before it's used for real. Rejected with a 400 listing every placeholder the template references that variables doesn't supply, and if the template is currently inactive.

post.summary: Enqueue an async bank statement import job
post.description: Sits alongside the existing synchronous bank reconciliation endpoints -- nothing here changes how those behave; this is an additional, queued entry point.

post.summary: Enqueue an async budget recalculation job
Enqueue an async dashboard cache refresh job
Enqueue an async report generation job

get.summary: List recent background job runs, optionally filtered by queue name or status
get.description: limit is silently capped at 200 regardless of what is requested (defaults to 50).

post.summary: Create a legal entity
post.description: code/name/legalName are required; baseCurrency, fiscalYearStartMonth, and isConsolidationParent all fall back to real server-side defaults when omitted. code must be unique.

get.summary: List every entity
get.description: Includes each entity's immediate subsidiaries, but not the full multi-level hierarchy chain — see GET /entities/:id/hierarchy for that.

get.summary: Get one entity, including its immediate subsidiaries and parent

patch.description: Partial update — every field is optional here even though most are required on create. Cannot clear parentEntityId back to null once set (omitting it leaves the existing value untouched, it does not accept an explicit null).

delete.description: Soft delete (isActive: false) — the row is never removed, and there is no corresponding reactivate endpoint.

get.summary: Walk this entity's full parent chain up to its top-level consolidation parent

post.summary: Create a group-chart account
post.description: Accounts are global to the group (one shared chart across every entity, not entity-scoped) — code must be unique across the whole chart.

get.summary: List group-chart accounts
get.description: Filterable by accountType and activeOnly; both optional.

get.summary: Get a group-chart account by id

delete.description: A soft delete (isActive=false) on the group-wide account itself — separate from, and does not affect, any entity's own per-entity activation via EntityAccount.

post.summary: Activate a group-chart account for use by one entity
post.description: Upserts the EntityAccount join row that makes a group-chart account postable for that specific entity — the group-chart account itself is created separately and shared across all entities.

get.summary: List an entity's own active (postable) accounts

post.summary: Create a project
post.description: Top of the Project → Phase → Block → Floor → Unit real-estate hierarchy. code is unique per entity, not globally.

get.summary: List projects
get.description: entityId is an optional filter; omit it to list every project across every entity.

get.summary: Get a project with its full hierarchy
get.description: One call returns every phase, block, floor, and unit nested underneath, not just the project row itself.

post.summary: Create a phase under a project
post.description: 404s if the parent project does not exist; code is unique per project, not globally.

post.summary: Create a block under a phase
post.description: 404s if the parent phase does not exist; code is unique per phase, not globally.

post.summary: Create a floor under a block
post.description: 404s if the parent block does not exist; code is unique per block, not globally.

post.summary: Create a unit under a floor
post.description: 404s if the parent floor does not exist; code is unique per floor, not globally. The bottom of the Project → Phase → Block → Floor → Unit hierarchy — this is the same Unit sold through Property Sales.

post.summary: Create a department
post.description: code is unique per entity, not globally.

get.summary: List departments
get.description: entityId is an optional filter; omit it to list every department across every entity.

post.summary: Create a cost center
post.description: code is unique per entity, not globally.

get.summary: List cost centers
get.description: entityId is an optional filter; omit it to list every cost center across every entity.

post.summary: Create a funding source
post.description: code is unique per entity, not globally.

get.summary: List funding sources
get.description: entityId is an optional filter; omit it to list every funding source across every entity.

post.summary: Create a vendor
post.description: code is globally unique — unlike every other dimension in this controller, vendors are NOT entity-scoped.

get.summary: List every vendor
get.description: No entityId filter exists — vendors are a single global list, not scoped per entity.

post.summary: Create a customer
post.description: code is globally unique — same non-entity-scoped shape as Vendors, not per-entity like Departments/Cost Centers/Funding Sources.

get.summary: List every customer
get.description: No entityId filter exists — customers are a single global list, not scoped per entity.

post.summary: Create a draft journal entry
post.description: Entity-scoped by RLS on entityId. The entry starts DRAFT and must go through submit → approve → post before it affects the ledger.

get.summary: List journal entries
get.description: Filterable by entityId, status, and fiscalPeriodId; all optional.

get.summary: Get a journal entry by id

post.summary: Submit a draft journal entry for approval
post.description: Only valid from DRAFT; moves the entry to PENDING_APPROVAL.

post.summary: Approve a pending journal entry
post.description: Only valid from PENDING_APPROVAL. The preparer of the entry cannot also approve it — enforced server-side, rejected with a 400 otherwise.

post.summary: Reject a pending journal entry
post.description: Only valid from PENDING_APPROVAL.

post.summary: Post an approved journal entry to the ledger
post.description: Only valid from APPROVED. Enforces balanced debits/credits and an open fiscal period inside one DB transaction; assigns the gap-free journal number.

post.summary: Reverse a posted journal entry
post.description: Only valid from POSTED. Creates a new, separate, auto-approved journal entry dated today (SYSTEM_REVERSAL, linked via reversalOfId) rather than mutating the original — the original stays in the ledger as posted history.

post.summary: Lock a fiscal period against further posting
post.description: Rejected with a 409 if any journal entry in the period is still DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL, or APPROVED-but-not-posted — every entry must be POSTED or REJECTED first.

get.summary: Get the trial balance for an entity
get.description: fiscalPeriodId is optional; omitting it returns the balance as of the current period.

post.summary: Record an intercompany transaction: the initiator's journal entry plus an automatic mirror entry on the counterparty's books
post.description: Both entries post as Dr due-from/Cr [account] on the initiator side and Dr [account]/Cr due-to on the mirror side, linked via one IntercompanyTransaction record for later reconciliation and consolidation elimination. Rejected if initiatorEntityId equals counterpartyEntityId, or if amount is not positive.

get.summary: List intercompany transactions, optionally filtered by entity (either side) or reconciliation status

post.summary: Reconcile an intercompany transaction pair
post.description: Marks RECONCILED only if both the initiator's entry and its mirror are POSTED; otherwise marks PARTIALLY_RECONCILED. Rejected with a 400 if no mirror entry was ever recorded for this transaction.

post.summary: Flag an intercompany transaction as DISPUTED
Create a consolidation group
post.description: Rejected if the code is already used, or if parentEntityId does not reference a real entity.

get.summary: List consolidation groups
get.description: Includes each group's own ownership rows.

post.summary: Record an ownership stake between a parent and child entity within a group
post.description: ownershipPercent must be between 0 and 100 (exclusive of 0). effectiveTo is optional — an open-ended stake.

get.summary: Consolidated trial balance for a group
get.description: Sums posted journal lines by account across every member entity (the parent plus every child ownership), then nets out this group's own recorded intercompany eliminations against the gross totals — eliminations are subtracted in aggregate, not matched back to individual accounts. Optionally scoped to one fiscal period.

get.summary: Consolidated profit & loss for a group
get.description: Derived from the same consolidated trial balance the trial-balance route returns, filtered to revenue/expense accounts. Minority interest is a SIMPLIFIED calculation: the group's total net income is distributed evenly across subsidiaries before applying each one's own minority percentage, not attributed per-subsidiary from its own actual results — a stated, real limitation, not full statutory minority-interest accounting.

get.summary: Consolidated balance sheet for a group
get.description: Also derived from the same consolidated trial balance, filtered to asset/liability/equity accounts. Includes a `balances` boolean (assets vs. liabilities+equity, within a small rounding tolerance) as a self-check on the result.

post.summary: Create an estate
post.description: Rejected if this code is already used by another estate in the same entity.

get.summary: List estates for an entity, with their projects
get.description: Row-level-security scoped by entity/businessUnit dimensions.

post.summary: Allocate (sell) a unit directly to a customer
post.description: The older, direct allocation path (pre-Phase-4), distinct from reserveUnit/convertReservation below. Rejected if the unit is not AVAILABLE or salePrice is not positive. Sets the unit to RESERVED (not ALLOCATED) and creates the allocation in one transaction.

post.summary: Force-set a unit's status
post.description: No transition guard of any kind — any status can be set from any current status. An administrative override, not a workflow action.

post.summary: Create an installment schedule for an allocation
post.description: Rejected if the allocation already has a schedule, or if the installments' amounts do not sum to the allocation's own salePrice (within 0.01).

get.summary: Get an allocation's installment schedule and lines
Get a customer's statement across every unit allocation
get.description: For each allocation: unit, sale price, status, and outstanding balance (total due minus total paid across its installment lines), plus a grand total outstanding across all of them.

post.summary: Reserve a unit for a customer
post.description: Rejected if the unit is not AVAILABLE or already has an ACTIVE reservation. expiresInHours defaults to 72 if omitted or not positive. Auto-flags the reservation as a resale if this unit has a prior cancelled allocation.

post.summary: Cancel a reservation
post.description: Rejected unless the reservation is currently ACTIVE. Returns the unit to AVAILABLE.

post.summary: Convert an active reservation into a confirmed sale
post.description: Rejected unless the reservation is ACTIVE and not yet expired. Creates the UnitSaleAllocation (status ALLOCATED), then raises and posts an AR invoice through the existing Accounts Receivable flow (no bespoke GL posting here).

post.summary: Expire every ACTIVE reservation past its expiry
post.description: Idempotent — safe to call repeatedly. Returns the affected units to AVAILABLE. Not currently wired to a scheduled worker job; this is the manual trigger until it is.

post.summary: Cancel a unit sale allocation
post.description: Rejected if already cancelled or already HANDED_OVER/SOLD. Returns the unit to AVAILABLE. Does NOT touch any AR invoice already posted for this allocation — a credit note/write-off is a separate, deliberate AR action this route does not perform.

post.summary: Transfer an allocation to a different customer, same unit
post.description: Rejected if the original is cancelled or already HANDED_OVER/SOLD. Cancels the original allocation and creates a new one linked via transferredFromAllocationId, rather than mutating the customer in place, so history survives. Any existing installment schedule/AR invoice stays attached to the original (now-cancelled) allocation — reassigning those is a separate, deliberate follow-up action this route does not perform.

post.summary: Swap the unit under an allocation, same customer
post.description: Rejected if the original allocation is cancelled/HANDED_OVER/SOLD, or the new unit is not AVAILABLE. Same lineage/limitations as transfer (installment schedule/AR invoice reassignment is a separate follow-up action). Frees the original unit to AVAILABLE.

get.summary: Get a unit's full allocation event history (reservations, sales, cancellations, transfers, swaps)
Reservation pipeline counts
get.description: active (currently ACTIVE), expiringSoon (ACTIVE and expiring within 48 hours), and convertedThisMonth/cancelledThisMonth (calendar-month-to-date, since the 1st of the current month).

post.summary: Create an AR invoice (DRAFT)
post.description: Each line's VAT (rate, amount, authority account) is resolved server-side from its own vatTaxCodeId, if supplied — not asked for directly.

get.summary: List AR invoices, optionally filtered by entity, customer, or status
Get a single AR invoice by id

post.summary: Post a DRAFT AR invoice to the GL
post.description: Posts Dr AR control (gross, including any output VAT) / Cr each line's own revenue account (ex-VAT) / Cr the relevant VAT authority account for any line with output VAT — only lines created with a vatTaxCodeId contribute a VAT credit. Writes a matching CustomerLedger INVOICE entry. Only DRAFT invoices are postable.

post.summary: Create a DRAFT receipt allocating a payment across one or more posted AR invoices
post.description: Every allocation's target invoice must belong to the same customer and already be POSTED, and the allocated amount cannot exceed that invoice's own open balance (its VAT-inclusive total less amountReceived, with a small rounding tolerance). Unlike AP payment vouchers, a receipt has no separate approval step — it goes straight from DRAFT to posting.

get.summary: Get a single receipt, with its invoice allocations

post.summary: Post a DRAFT receipt to the GL and apply it against its allocated invoices
post.description: Posts Dr Cash / Cr AR control for the receipt's total allocated amount. Increments amountReceived on every allocated invoice and writes one CustomerLedger RECEIPT entry.

get.summary: AR aging report: open posted invoices bucketed by days past due
get.description: Buckets are current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+, computed from each invoice's own due date against asOfDate (defaults to today).

get.summary: Posted revenue (invoiced) and receipts grouped by project, for an optional date range
get.description: Invoice lines with no projectId roll up under "Unassigned". Each invoice's own total receipts are apportioned across its lines pro-rata by line value — there is no per-line receipt allocation in the underlying data, so this is an estimate, not a directly-recorded figure.

get.summary: Overdue Real Estate mortgage installment lines, for AR-side visibility
get.description: Reads InstallmentLine (Real Estate mortgage schedules), not ARInvoice — a genuinely different model, surfaced here so AR staff can see customer-facing overdue amounts that never went through an AR invoice at all.

get.summary: Customer statement: every ledger entry for a customer within an optional date range, with a running balance
get.description: Running balance accumulates as debit minus credit per entry, in transactionDate order.

post.summary: Register a new land parcel
post.description: 409 if the code is already used by another parcel for the same entity.

get.summary: List land parcels
get.description: RLS-scoped to the caller's entity/business-unit access; optionally further filtered by entityId and status. Each parcel includes its acquisitions, title deeds, survey plans, and plots.

get.summary: Get a land parcel
get.description: Includes acquisitions, title deeds, survey plans, and plots (each plot with its own project-release record, if any). 404 if the parcel does not exist.

post.summary: Record a land acquisition against a parcel
post.description: 404 if the parcel does not exist. Sets the parcel to UNDER_ACQUISITION as a side effect.

patch.summary: Set a land acquisition's status directly
patch.description: 404 if not found; 400 once the acquisition is COMPLETED — use the dedicated complete route to reach that status instead.

post.summary: Complete a land acquisition
post.description: 404 if not found; 409 if already COMPLETED; 400 if CANCELLED. Sets the parcel to ACQUIRED. Capitalizing the acquisition cost to a GL asset account is deliberately out of scope here — deferred to the Fixed Assets module's own Construction-in-Progress handling once that exists.

post.summary: Add a title deed to a parcel
post.description: 404 if the parcel does not exist. Created as IN_PROGRESS. Moves the parcel to IN_TITLING unless it's already TITLED.

post.summary: Mark a title deed as perfected
post.description: 404 if not found; 409 if already PERFECTED. Sets the parcel to TITLED.

post.summary: Reject a title deed
post.description: 404 if not found. The reason is appended to the title's own notes field, not stored on a dedicated rejection-reason column.

get.summary: List title deeds for a parcel

post.summary: Create a survey plan for a parcel
post.description: 404 if the parcel does not exist; 409 if the plan number is already used for this parcel. Created as SUBMITTED.

post.summary: Approve a survey plan
post.description: 404 if not found; 409 if already APPROVED. Sets the parcel to SURVEYED.

post.summary: Reject a survey plan
post.description: 404 if not found. The reason is not persisted on the record itself — it's captured only via the automatic audit trail on this request.

get.summary: List survey plans for a parcel

post.summary: Subdivide a parcel into plots against an approved survey plan
post.description: Requires at least one plot. The survey plan must belong to this parcel and be APPROVED. The sum of plot areas cannot exceed the parcel area. Creates every plot as AVAILABLE and sets the parcel to SUBDIVIDED.

get.summary: List plots for a parcel
get.description: Optionally filtered by status.

patch.description: 404 if not found. Not guarded by any status-transition rule — any value can be set from any current status.

post.summary: Create a new master plan version for an estate
post.description: 404 if the estate does not exist. The version number auto-increments from the highest existing version for this estate (starting at 1). Zones are optional and created inline if provided.

get.summary: List master plan versions for an estate, newest first
Get a master plan version, including its zones
get.description: 404 if not found.

post.summary: Approve a master plan version
post.description: 404 if not found; 409 if already APPROVED; 400 if SUPERSEDED. Whichever other version of this estate's plan is currently APPROVED (if any) is automatically moved to SUPERSEDED in the same transaction — only one version can be APPROVED per estate at a time.

post.summary: Release a plot to a project (Land Bank -> Real Estate hand-off)
post.description: 404 if the plot or project does not exist; 400 if the plot is not AVAILABLE; 409 if the plot already has an active (non-cancelled) release. Re-releasing a plot whose prior release was cancelled updates that same release record rather than creating a new one. Sets the plot to ALLOCATED.

post.summary: Cancel a plot's active project release
post.description: 404 if there is no active release for this plot. Sets the plot back to AVAILABLE.

get.summary: List active (non-cancelled) plot releases for a project
get.description: Each release includes its own plot record.

post.summary: Create a lead
post.description: Sends a best-effort assignment notification to assignedToId if given (a notification failure never blocks lead creation).

get.summary: List leads
get.description: Row-level-security scoped by entity/businessUnit dimensions, then optionally filtered by entityId/status/assignedToId.

get.summary: Get a lead, with its assignee, activity history, and linked prospect if converted

post.summary: Reassign a lead
post.description: Sends a best-effort "assigned to you" notification to the new assignee only if assignedToId actually changes, not on a no-op reassignment to the same person.

post.summary: Mark a lead qualified and ready to convert
post.description: Rejected if the lead has already CONVERTED or is DISQUALIFIED. (NEW -> CONTACTED happens implicitly on the first logged activity, not through this route — see the activities endpoints.)

post.summary: Disqualify a lead
post.description: Rejected only if the lead has already CONVERTED; allowed from any other status, including a lead that is already disqualified.

post.summary: Convert a qualified lead into a Prospect
post.description: One transaction: marks the lead CONVERTED and creates a linked Prospect (1:1). Rejected if the lead has already converted, is disqualified, or already has a linked prospect. Does not touch Customer/Reservation — that only happens later, when the resulting prospect reserves a unit.

post.summary: Log an activity against a lead
post.description: If this is the first activity logged on a lead still in NEW status, the lead is automatically advanced to CONTACTED as a side effect.

post.summary: Create a prospect directly (not via lead conversion)
post.description: existingCustomerId, if given, must reference a real Customer (rejected otherwise). Sends a best-effort assignment notification if assignedToId is given.

get.summary: List prospects
get.description: Row-level-security scoped by entity/businessUnit dimensions, then optionally filtered by entityId/status/assignedToId.

get.summary: Get a prospect, with its assignee, linked lead, unit of interest, converted customer, and activity history

post.summary: Mark a site visit scheduled for a prospect
post.description: Rejected if the prospect is already WON or LOST.

post.summary: Mark a scheduled site visit done
post.description: Rejected if the prospect is already WON or LOST.

post.summary: Move a prospect into negotiation
post.description: Rejected if the prospect is already WON or LOST.

post.summary: Mark a prospect lost
post.description: Rejected if the prospect is already WON or LOST.

post.summary: Mark a prospect won
post.description: Rejected unless the prospect is currently RESERVED — a stricter gate than the other prospect-status routes (which only reject WON/LOST). Does not itself touch the sale allocation; it only closes out the CRM record once a sale has been confirmed elsewhere.

post.summary: Reserve a unit for a prospect
post.description: Uses realestate.sell, not crm.manage, unlike every other route in this controller. Delegates to the existing Real Estate unit-reservation flow rather than reimplementing it; creates a Customer first if the prospect doesn't already have one converted. On success, marks the prospect RESERVED.

post.summary: Log an activity against a prospect
post.description: Unlike the equivalent lead-activity route, this has no side effect on the prospect's own status.

get.summary: List upcoming/overdue follow-ups across leads and prospects
get.description: withinHours defaults to 48 when not given. Optionally filtered to one assignee.

get.summary: CRM pipeline analytics: lead/prospect counts by status and source, plus won/lost this month
get.description: leadConversionRate is convertedLeads/totalLeads (0 if there are no leads). wonThisMonth/lostThisMonth are calendar-month-to-date counts (since the 1st of the current month), not a rolling 30-day window.

post.summary: Create a mortgage application against a unit sale allocation
post.description: Rejected if the allocation does not exist. Starts in DRAFT.

get.summary: List mortgage applications
get.description: Row-level-security scoped by entity/businessUnit dimensions, then optionally filtered by entityId/status.

get.summary: Get a mortgage application, with its allocation

post.summary: Submit a mortgage application for approval
post.description: Rejected unless the application is currently DRAFT.

post.summary: Approve a submitted mortgage application
post.description: Rejected unless the application is currently SUBMITTED. interestRatePercent/tenorMonths fall back to the application's own originally-requested values when not given in the approval.

post.summary: Decline a submitted mortgage application
post.description: Rejected unless the application is currently SUBMITTED.

post.summary: Disburse an approved mortgage
post.description: Uses revenue.recognize, not mortgage.manage, unlike every other route in this controller (the same pattern HandoverController's own :id/complete route uses). Rejected unless the application is currently APPROVED, or if disbursedAmount exceeds the approved amount. Records the disbursement as an ordinary customer payment against the sale's installment schedule, reusing the existing Revenue Recognition module rather than duplicating GL posting logic here — the mortgage bank account is treated as just another source of cash.

post.summary: Close a disbursed mortgage application
post.description: Rejected unless the application is currently DISBURSED.

get.summary: Mortgage pipeline counts and exposure totals
get.description: byStatus is a count per MortgageStatus value present in the (optionally entityId-filtered) result set. totalOutstanding is totalAmountApproved minus totalDisbursed, not a separately-tracked balance.

post.summary: Record a customer installment payment (deferred-revenue posting)
post.description: Posts Dr Bank / Cr Deferred Revenue for the payment. entityId is NOT part of the request body — it is derived server-side from the installment line and access-checked, not client-supplied.

post.summary: Recognize revenue on unit handover
post.description: Posts Dr Deferred Revenue / Cr Property Sales Revenue and Dr Cost of Sales / Cr Property Inventory in the same call — the second half of the IFRS 15 deferred-revenue pattern this module implements (see customer-payments for the first half).

post.summary: Schedule a handover for a unit sale allocation
post.description: Rejected if the allocation does not exist, or already has a handover record (one handover record per allocation).

get.summary: List handover records
get.description: Row-level-security scoped by entity/businessUnit dimensions, then optionally filtered by status/entityId.

get.summary: Get a handover record, with its unit, customer, allocation, and snags

post.summary: Record the handover inspection as done
post.description: Rejected if the handover is already COMPLETED or CANCELLED.

post.summary: Cancel a handover
post.description: Rejected if the handover is already COMPLETED or CANCELLED.

post.summary: Complete a handover
post.description: Uses revenue.recognize, not handover.manage, unlike every other route in this controller. Rejected if the handover is already COMPLETED/CANCELLED, or if any of its snags is still OPEN or IN_PROGRESS. Reuses the existing Revenue Recognition module (recognizeOnHandover) for the GL entry and the unit/allocation status flip to HANDED_OVER — no posting logic duplicated here.

post.summary: Report a snag (defect) against a handover
post.description: severity defaults to MINOR and source to HANDOVER_INSPECTION when omitted. Sends a best-effort notification to assignedToId if given (never blocks snag creation). Side effect: if the handover is currently INSPECTION_DONE, it moves to SNAGS_PENDING.

get.summary: List snags for a handover record, optionally filtered by status
Get snag counts by status and by severity for a handover record
List snags, optionally filtered by unit and/or status
get.description: Not scoped to one handover record — spans every handover, unlike HandoverController's own :id/snags.

post.summary: Mark a snag in progress
post.description: No status guard — callable from any current status.

post.summary: Mark a snag resolved
post.description: No status guard — callable from any current status.

post.summary: Verify a resolved snag
post.description: Rejected unless the snag is currently RESOLVED — the only snag-transition route in this controller with a status guard.

post.summary: Reject a snag
post.description: No status guard — callable from any current status.

get.summary: Get the caller's own statement across every unit allocation
get.description: Pure delegation to RealEstateService.getCustomerStatement (the same method the internal realestate.view route already uses) — for each allocation: unit, sale price, status, and outstanding balance (total due minus total paid across its installment lines, each installment line included), plus a grand total outstanding across all of them.

get.summary: List the caller's own handover records
get.description: Every handover record for this customer, newest scheduled-date first, each including its own unit and snag items (newest first) — lets a customer track handover/inspection/snag-resolution progress on their own unit(s) without a staff member in the loop.

post.summary: Create a tenant (occupy a unit)
post.description: 404 if the unit or an active customer does not exist; 409 if the unit already has an ACTIVE tenant. Created as ACTIVE.

get.summary: List tenants
get.description: RLS-scoped to the caller's entity/business-unit access; optionally filtered by entityId, unitId, and status. Each tenant includes its customer and unit.

get.summary: Get a tenant
get.description: 404 if not found. Includes customer, unit, and all leases (newest first).

post.summary: End a tenancy
post.description: 404 if not found; 409 unless the tenancy is currently ACTIVE; 400 if the tenant still has a DRAFT or ACTIVE lease — terminate the lease first. Sets the tenant to FORMER.

post.summary: Create a lease for a tenant
post.description: 404 if the tenant does not exist; 400 unless the tenant is ACTIVE, or if the lease's own unitId does not match the unit the tenant occupies; 409 if the lease number is already used for this entity, or if the unit already has a DRAFT or ACTIVE lease. Created as DRAFT.

get.summary: List leases
get.description: RLS-scoped to the caller's entity/business-unit access; optionally filtered by entityId, tenantId, and status. Each lease includes its tenant (with customer) and unit.

get.summary: Get a lease
get.description: 404 if not found. Includes the tenant (with customer), unit, and every rent invoice (with its own AR invoice), newest period first.

post.summary: Activate a lease
post.description: 404 if not found; 409 unless the lease is currently DRAFT.

post.summary: Renew a lease
post.description: 404 if not found; 409 unless the lease is currently ACTIVE or EXPIRED. Sets the lease back to ACTIVE with the new end date; the rent amount is only changed if a new one is supplied, otherwise it stays the same.

post.summary: Mark a lease as expired
post.description: 404 if not found; 409 unless the lease is currently ACTIVE.

post.summary: Terminate a lease early
post.description: 404 if not found; 409 unless the lease is currently DRAFT or ACTIVE. terminatedAt defaults to now if not supplied.

post.summary: Generate a rent invoice for one period of an active lease
post.description: 404 if the lease does not exist; 409 unless it is currently ACTIVE. Creates a DRAFT AR invoice for the period via the Accounts Receivable module and links it to the lease — no GL posting logic is duplicated here; use the post route separately to post it.

post.summary: Post a generated rent invoice to the GL
post.description: 404 if the rent-invoice link does not exist. Delegates to the Accounts Receivable module's own posting logic — no separate posting path for rent.

get.summary: Lease portfolio counts and rent-roll total
get.description: expiringWithin60Days counts ACTIVE leases whose endDate falls within 60 days. monthlyRentRoll sums only ACTIVE leases with rentFrequency MONTHLY — QUARTERLY/ANNUALLY leases are deliberately excluded (the service's own comment states this is pending frequency normalization, not an oversight), so this figure understates total rent roll wherever non-monthly leases exist.

post.summary: Create a facility
post.description: Must be linked to either a projectId (a common-area asset) or a unitId (an in-unit asset) — rejected if neither is given.

get.summary: List facilities
get.description: RLS-scoped to the caller; entityId, status, projectId, and unitId are all optional filters. Each facility's own nested maintenanceRequests only includes OPEN/ASSIGNED/IN_PROGRESS/ON_HOLD ones — unlike getFacility, which includes every request regardless of status.

get.summary: Get a facility by id, with every maintenance request against it
get.description: Unlike findFacilities' own nested list, this includes requests of every status, not just the open ones.

post.summary: Record a completed service visit
post.description: Rejected if the facility is DECOMMISSIONED. Sets status back to OPERATIONAL regardless of what it was before (e.g. clears OUT_OF_SERVICE).

post.summary: Mark a facility out of service
post.description: Rejected if the facility is already DECOMMISSIONED.

post.summary: Send a facility for decommission approval
post.description: Only valid from OPERATIONAL, UNDER_MAINTENANCE, or OUT_OF_SERVICE, and rejected if a decommission request is already in progress for this facility. Starts a Workflow Engine instance; the facility's own status is left untouched until refreshDecommission is called and the workflow resolves.

post.summary: Poll the linked decommission workflow instance
post.description: A no-op if there is no workflow in progress. If the workflow is APPROVED, moves the facility to DECOMMISSIONED. If REJECTED or RETURNED, clears the workflow link and leaves the facility's prior status untouched — a rejected decommission does not change its operational state.

post.summary: Raise a maintenance request
post.description: If facilityId is given, rejected when that facility is DECOMMISSIONED. priority defaults to MEDIUM and source to INTERNAL when omitted. Starts OPEN.

get.summary: List maintenance requests
get.description: RLS-scoped to the caller; entityId, status, facilityId, unitId, and tenantId are all optional filters.

get.summary: Get a maintenance dashboard aggregate
get.description: Request counts by status, open-request counts by priority, and a count of facilities currently UNDER_MAINTENANCE. entityId is an optional filter. Reused by DashboardService/ReportingService rather than re-queried there.

get.summary: Get a maintenance request by id

post.summary: Assign a maintenance request to a vendor
post.description: Only valid from OPEN. Side effect: if the linked facility is currently OPERATIONAL, it's also moved to UNDER_MAINTENANCE.

post.summary: Move an assigned request to IN_PROGRESS
post.description: Only valid from ASSIGNED.

post.summary: Place a request on hold
post.description: Only valid from ASSIGNED or IN_PROGRESS.

post.summary: Resume a held request
post.description: Only valid from ON_HOLD. Moves directly to IN_PROGRESS, not back to ASSIGNED.

post.summary: Mark a request resolved
post.description: Only valid from ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, or ON_HOLD.

post.summary: Close a resolved request
post.description: Only valid from RESOLVED. Side effect: if the linked facility is currently UNDER_MAINTENANCE, it's restored to OPERATIONAL.

post.summary: Cancel a request
post.description: Only valid from OPEN, ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, or ON_HOLD — the same open-status set used to scope findFacilities' own nested include, not just OPEN alone.

post.summary: Bill the assigned vendor for a maintenance request
post.description: Requires an assigned vendor and is rejected if the request has already been billed, or if its status is anything other than RESOLVED or CLOSED. Uses actualCost if set, falling back to costEstimate. Reuses AccountsPayableService.createInvoice() wholesale to create a real VendorInvoice — posting that invoice to the GL remains a separate step on the existing POST /accounts-payable/invoices/:id/post route, not done here.

post.summary: Create a workflow definition
post.description: code must be unique (409 if not); stage sequence numbers must be unique within the definition (400 if not). workflowRules reference a stage by its own sequence number, not its id, since the id does not exist yet at request time.

get.summary: List workflow definitions
get.description: entityType is an optional filter.

get.summary: Get a workflow definition by code, with its stages and rules

post.summary: Start a workflow instance for an entity
post.description: Rejected (409) if the workflow is not active. Any stage with a workflow-level rule targeting it is included only if at least one of those rules matches the supplied context — a definition with rules can produce instances with genuinely different stage sets depending on context, not always the full stage list. 400 if no stage ends up applicable at all.

get.summary: List workflow instances for one entity
get.description: entityType and entityId are both required, not optional filters — this route always scopes to exactly one entity.

get.summary: Get a workflow instance, with every stage instance and every action taken on it

post.summary: Act on the currently-active stage of a workflow instance
post.description: 409 if the instance isn't IN_PROGRESS or has no active stage. Role-gated by the active stage's own requiredRoleCode for every action except COMMENT (400 if the caller lacks it). A REJECT action ends the WHOLE instance immediately, not just the current stage — there is no per-stage-only rejection.

post.summary: Resubmit a RETURNED instance
post.description: Rejected (409) unless the instance is currently RETURNED. Always restarts from the FIRST stage, not the stage it was returned from — a RETURN sends the whole approval chain back to the beginning, not just back one step.

post.summary: Create a vendor invoice (DRAFT)

get.summary: List vendor invoices, optionally filtered by entity, vendor, or status
Get a single vendor invoice by id

post.summary: Post a DRAFT, non-PO vendor invoice to the GL
post.description: Only invoices with no purchaseOrderId can post here — a PO-backed invoice must post through Procurement's own three-way match instead. Only DRAFT invoices are postable. Debits each line's own account for quantity times unit cost, credits the supplied AP control account for the total, and writes a matching VendorLedger INVOICE entry.

post.summary: Create a DRAFT payment batch for a given entity and batch number
Approve a DRAFT payment batch
post.description: The preparer who created the batch cannot also approve it — segregation of duties, enforced server-side.

post.summary: Post every APPROVED voucher in an APPROVED batch, then close the batch
post.description: Iterates every voucher currently in the batch; only vouchers already at APPROVED status are posted (others are silently skipped, not rejected). Sets the batch itself to PROCESSED once done.

post.summary: Create a DRAFT payment voucher allocating a payment across one or more posted vendor invoices
post.description: Every allocation's target invoice must belong to the same vendor and already be POSTED, and the allocated amount cannot exceed that invoice's own open balance (its total less amountPaid, with a small rounding tolerance). WHT/VAT for each allocation can be supplied either as a taxCodeId (resolved to a rate and authority account server-side) or as an explicit rate plus authority account directly.

get.summary: Get a single payment voucher, with its allocations and any WHT/VAT deductions

post.summary: Approve a DRAFT payment voucher
post.description: The preparer who created the voucher cannot also approve it — segregation of duties, enforced server-side.

post.summary: Post an APPROVED payment voucher to the GL and apply it against its allocated invoices
post.description: Posts Dr AP control (gross allocated) / Cr Cash (net of WHT+VAT) / Cr WHT payable / Cr VAT payable, the tax-payable lines grouped by tax authority account since different allocations may use different accounts. Increments amountPaid on every allocated invoice and writes one VendorLedger PAYMENT entry.

post.summary: Remit a PENDING WHT deduction to the tax authority
post.description: Posts Dr tax authority payable / Cr the supplied cash account, then marks the deduction REMITTED. Rejected if the deduction has already been remitted.

post.summary: Remit a PENDING VAT deduction to the tax authority
post.description: Posts Dr tax authority payable / Cr the supplied cash account, then marks the deduction REMITTED. Rejected if the deduction has already been remitted.

get.summary: Vendor aging report: open posted invoices bucketed by days past due
get.description: Buckets are current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+, computed from each invoice's own due date against asOfDate (defaults to today).

get.summary: List open posted invoices due on or before throughDate (defaults to today)
Forecast total cash required to clear every invoice due within the next N days (default 30)
List WHT deductions for an entity, optionally filtered by remittance status
List VAT deductions for an entity, optionally filtered by remittance status
Vendor statement: every ledger entry for a vendor within an optional date range, with a running balance
get.description: Running balance accumulates as credit minus debit per entry, in transactionDate order.

post.summary: Create a warehouse for an entity

get.summary: List warehouses
get.description: RLS-scoped to the caller's entity access; optionally further filtered by entityId.

post.summary: Create a stock item (a warehouse-trackable SKU)
post.description: domain (e.g. construction materials vs consumables) partitions the catalog for filtering — it does not affect how movements/valuation work.

get.summary: List stock items
get.description: RLS-scoped to the caller's entity access; optionally further filtered by entityId and/or domain.

get.summary: Get on-hand quantity and average unit cost for one item at one warehouse

post.summary: Create a draft goods receipt
Post a draft goods receipt
post.description: Increases on-hand quantity for every line and recomputes each item's weighted-average unit cost.

post.summary: Create a draft material issue
Post a draft material issue
post.description: Rejects with 400 if any line would take on-hand quantity negative — there is no backorder/negative-stock concept.

post.summary: Create a draft transfer between two warehouses
Post a draft stock transfer
post.description: Same insufficient-stock rejection as posting a material issue applies to the source warehouse.

post.summary: Create a draft physical stock count
Post a draft stock count
post.description: Only lines whose counted-vs-system variance exceeds a small tolerance produce an adjustment movement — negligible variances are silently skipped, not adjusted to zero.

post.summary: Create a draft Bill of Quantities for a project

get.summary: List BOQs
get.description: RLS-scoped to the caller's project access; optionally further filtered by projectId.

post.summary: Advance (or reject) a BOQ's workflow status
post.description: Shared with every other PMO document type: DRAFT -> REVIEWED -> APPROVED -> CERTIFIED, one step at a time only — skipping a step is rejected with 409. REJECTED is reachable from any status as the one exception to the one-step rule.

post.summary: Create a draft work package under a BOQ's project

get.summary: List work packages
get.description: RLS-scoped to the caller's project access; optionally further filtered by projectId.

post.summary: Advance (or reject) a work package's workflow status
post.description: Same shared one-step DRAFT -> REVIEWED -> APPROVED -> CERTIFIED workflow as POST /pmo/boqs/:id/advance.

post.summary: Create a draft progress valuation for a work package
post.description: valuationNumber is computed server-side (previous valuation's number + 1) and is never a request field.

get.summary: List progress valuations for a work package, including each one's certificate if it has one

post.summary: Advance (or reject) a progress valuation's workflow status
post.description: Same shared one-step DRAFT -> REVIEWED -> APPROVED -> CERTIFIED workflow as POST /pmo/boqs/:id/advance. A valuation must be APPROVED before a certificate can be generated against it.

post.summary: Generate an interim payment certificate against an approved progress valuation
post.description: The referenced progress valuation must be APPROVED and must not already have a certificate — 409 otherwise. grossValuationAmount/retentionAmount/previousCertifiedAmount/netPayableAmount are all computed server-side, never request fields.

post.summary: Advance (or reject) a certificate's workflow status
post.description: Same shared one-step DRAFT -> REVIEWED -> APPROVED -> CERTIFIED workflow as POST /pmo/boqs/:id/advance. Reaching CERTIFIED also rolls this certificate's own retentionAmount into the work package's running Retention record as a side effect.

post.summary: Create a draft variation order against a work package

get.summary: List variation orders for a work package

post.summary: Advance (or reject) a variation order's workflow status
post.description: Same shared one-step DRAFT -> REVIEWED -> APPROVED -> CERTIFIED workflow as POST /pmo/boqs/:id/advance. Only APPROVED and CERTIFIED variation orders count toward a final account's totalVariations.

get.summary: Get a work package's retention record, including its release history
get.description: 404 if no certificate has reached CERTIFIED for this work package yet — the retention record is created as a side effect of that, not on work package creation.

post.summary: Release (part of) a work package's held retention
post.description: amount is a partial or full release, not a replacement value — rejected with 400 if it would exceed the retention's own remaining available amount (totalHeld minus what's already been released).

post.summary: Compute and create the final account for a work package
post.description: One-shot — 409 if a final account already exists for this work package. finalAccountAmount = the work package's own budgetAmount plus the sum of every APPROVED/CERTIFIED variation order; totalCertified is taken from the single latest CERTIFIED certificate's own grossValuationAmount, not summed across every certificate.

post.summary: Advance (or reject) a final account's workflow status
post.description: Same shared one-step DRAFT -> REVIEWED -> APPROVED -> CERTIFIED workflow as POST /pmo/boqs/:id/advance.

post.summary: Create a project task (WBS item)

get.summary: List project tasks
get.description: projectId and status are both optional filters.

get.summary: Get a task by id, including its own child tasks and dependency edges

post.summary: Update a task's percent complete
post.description: Status is derived automatically from percentComplete, not settable directly here: 0 -> NOT_STARTED, 1-99 -> IN_PROGRESS, 100 -> COMPLETED (stamping actualEnd if not already set). Rejected with a 409 on a CANCELLED task.

post.summary: Set a task's status directly
post.description: Unlike POST :id/progress, this sets status without touching percentComplete — no guard against setting a status inconsistent with the current progress value.

post.summary: Add a dependency between two tasks
post.description: Both tasks must belong to the same project. Rejected if the dependency already exists, or if it would create a cycle in the task network (checked via a graph reachability search, not assumed absent).

get.summary: Compute the critical path for a project
get.description: Classic forward/backward-pass CPM. Every dependency type is treated as "successor cannot start before predecessor + lag" for this calculation — a documented simplification; the four distinct relationship types (FINISH_TO_START etc.) are stored faithfully but this release's float math does not distinguish between them. Persists isCritical/totalFloatDays on every task as a side effect of computing them.

get.summary: Get Gantt-chart-shaped task and dependency data for a project
Compute PV/EV/AC/SV/CV/SPI/CPI earned-value metrics for a project
get.description: asOfDate is optional, defaulting to now. PV time-phases each task's budgetedCost linearly across its planned duration (a documented simplification, not S-curve-weighted). SPI/CPI are null rather than a divide-by-zero artifact when PV/AC is 0.

post.summary: Create a project risk
post.description: probability/impact default to MEDIUM when omitted; riskScore is computed server-side from the two.

get.summary: List risks
get.description: projectId and status are both optional filters; RLS-scoped to the caller regardless.

get.summary: Get a risk/issue counts-and-priorities summary
get.description: projectId is optional. The underlying service also supports an entityId filter, but this route does not expose it — only projectId is accepted here.

get.summary: Get a risk by id

post.summary: Record a risk assessment
post.description: Sets probability/impact and recomputes riskScore. Auto-advances status from IDENTIFIED to ASSESSED; leaves any other status unchanged. Rejected once the risk is CLOSED.

post.summary: Assign or change the risk owner
post.description: Notifies the new owner (best-effort) only when the ownerId actually changes.

post.summary: Set the risk mitigation plan
post.description: Forces status to MITIGATING regardless of the risk's current status (other than CLOSED, which is rejected).

post.summary: Move a risk to MONITORING
Close a risk
post.description: Terminal. Valid from any non-CLOSED status — unlike Issue's own close route below, there is no RESOLVED-first requirement.

post.summary: Convert a risk into a linked issue
post.description: One transaction: marks the risk OCCURRED and creates a new ProjectIssue (linked via riskId) through the same path — including the same assignment notification — as the issue create route below.

post.summary: Create a project issue
post.description: Notifies assignedToId (best-effort) if set at creation.

get.summary: List issues
get.description: projectId and status are both optional filters; RLS-scoped to the caller regardless.

get.summary: Get an issue by id

post.summary: Assign or reassign the issue
post.description: Notifies the new assignee (best-effort) only when assignedToId actually changes.

post.summary: Move an issue to IN_PROGRESS
Move an issue to ESCALATED
Resolve an issue
post.description: Sets RESOLVED and stamps resolvedAt; resolutionNotes is optional.

post.summary: Close an issue
post.description: Only valid from RESOLVED — rejected with a 400 stating the current status otherwise. A real, different guard shape from Risk's own close route above, which allows closing from any non-CLOSED status.

post.summary: Register a project resource (a labour crew or a piece of equipment)

get.summary: List project resources
get.description: projectId and type are both optional filters. isActive is not exposed as a filter here despite the underlying service supporting it — every resource, active or not, is currently returned.

get.summary: Get per-resource utilization for a project
get.description: Committed quantity (PLANNED+ACTIVE allocations) against capacity, per active resource. A resource with no capacity set reports utilizationPct as null rather than a misleading 0% or 100%.

get.summary: Get a resource by id, including its own allocation history

post.summary: Deactivate a resource
Reactivate a previously deactivated resource
Allocate a resource to a task
post.description: Rejects the allocation if it would over-book the resource: the sum of plannedQuantity across every PLANNED/ACTIVE allocation whose date range overlaps this one (including this request) is checked against the resource's own capacity. Resources with no capacity set skip this check entirely — capacity is opt-in, not assumed.

get.summary: List resource allocations
get.description: resourceId, taskId, and status are all optional filters.

get.summary: Get an allocation by id, including its own resource and task

post.summary: Start a PLANNED allocation
post.description: Rejected with a 409 if the allocation is already COMPLETED or CANCELLED.

post.summary: Complete an allocation
post.description: actualQuantity is optional — defaults to the allocation's own plannedQuantity if omitted. Rejected with a 409 if the allocation is already COMPLETED or CANCELLED.

post.summary: Cancel an allocation
post.description: Rejected with a 409 if the allocation is already COMPLETED or CANCELLED.

post.summary: Create a bank account for an entity

get.summary: List bank accounts
get.description: accountNumber is masked for callers without the unmask permission for the bankDetails field group.

post.summary: Create a petty-cash/custodian cash account for an entity

get.summary: List cash accounts for an entity

post.summary: Create a loan facility

get.summary: List loan facilities
get.description: facilityAmount and interestRatePercent are masked for callers without the unmask permission for the loanValues field group.

get.summary: Get a loan facility's current position
get.description: Computed on the fly from the facility's drawdowns, repayment schedule, and interest accruals — not a stored balance. Returns facilityAmount, totalDrawn, undrawnBalance, outstanding principal and interest.

post.summary: Draw down against a loan facility
post.description: Rejected if the facility is not ACTIVE, or if the drawdown would exceed the undrawn balance (facilityAmount minus prior drawdowns).

post.summary: Generate a flat-interest repayment schedule for a facility
post.description: Equal principal installments; interest on each installment is computed on the ORIGINAL total drawn balance (flat-rate, not declining-balance). Rejected if a schedule already exists for this facility, or if nothing has been drawn down yet.

post.summary: Record a repayment against one installment
post.description: Rejected if the installment was already fully paid, or if the principal/interest paid would exceed the amount due on that installment. The installment is marked settled once both principal and interest match what was due.

post.summary: Record an interest accrual against a loan facility
Create an investment placement
post.description: Rejected if principalAmount is not positive, or if maturityDate is not after placementDate.

get.summary: List investment placements, optionally filtered by entity and/or status

post.summary: Process a placement reaching maturity
post.description: Behavior depends on the placement's own maturityInstruction: PAYOUT marks it MATURED and stops there. Either rollover instruction marks the original MATURED AND creates a brand-new ACTIVE placement of the same tenor length, with its principal equal to the original principal (ROLLOVER_PRINCIPAL) or original principal plus actualInterestEarned (ROLLOVER_PRINCIPAL_AND_INTEREST). Returns the NEW placement in the rollover case, not the matured one. Rejected if the placement is not currently ACTIVE.

post.summary: Create an asset category
post.description: Depreciation method/useful life defaults for assets assigned to this category.

get.summary: List asset categories

post.summary: Register a fixed asset
post.description: assetTag must be unique per entity. residualValue defaults to 0 and can never exceed acquisitionCost.

get.summary: List fixed assets
get.description: entityId and status are both optional filters; RLS-scoped to the caller regardless.

get.summary: Get fixed asset register totals for an entity
Get a fixed asset by id

post.summary: Run depreciation for a period, for every active asset of an entity
post.description: A single batch call, not per-asset — processes every ACTIVE asset of the given entity acquired on or before the period, skipping any that are not due (each result line states its own outcome, including a skip reason where relevant).

post.summary: Dispose a fixed asset
post.description: Terminal — rejected if already disposed. Computes gain/loss as disposalProceeds minus net book value at disposal (acquisition cost less accumulated depreciation) and posts it.

post.summary: Create a tax code (WHT or VAT rate)

get.summary: List tax codes
get.description: taxType filter is optional; omit for both WHT and VAT.

get.summary: Get the WHT/VAT position for a date range
get.description: Period-bounded (periodStart/periodEnd required) — every WHT/VAT line in that window, any status, not just pending.

get.summary: Get the current outstanding WHT/VAT for an entity
get.description: Unbounded by date — every still-PENDING WHT/VAT line as of now, the dashboard-style counterpart to the period-bounded position endpoint above.

post.summary: Remit all WHT/VAT for a period in one action
post.description: Computes the same position getTaxPosition would for the given range, then settles every line in it — a single server-side computation over many tax lines, not a per-line action.

post.summary: Create a salary structure
post.description: code must be unique within the entity. basicSalary must be positive.

get.summary: List salary structures
get.description: entityId is an optional filter on top of RLS entity scoping. Salary component fields are masked for callers without the matching unmask permission.

post.summary: Create an employee master record
post.description: employeeCode must be unique within the entity.

get.summary: List active employees
get.description: entityId is an optional filter on top of RLS entity/department scoping. Bank details and tax/pension ids are each masked separately for callers without the matching unmask permission.

post.summary: Create a payroll run for a pay period
post.description: One run per (entityId, payPeriodName) — rejected with a 409 on a duplicate. Starts DRAFT.

post.summary: Calculate payslips for a DRAFT payroll run
post.description: One payslip per active employee in the run's own entity who has a salary structure assigned. Rejected with a 409 if the run isn't DRAFT, or a 400 if no eligible employee exists. Safe to re-run while still DRAFT — payslips are upserted, not duplicated. Advances the run to CALCULATED.

post.summary: Approve a CALCULATED payroll run
post.description: Rejected with a 409 if the run isn't currently CALCULATED. Advances the run to APPROVED.

post.summary: Post an APPROVED payroll run to the general ledger
post.description: Rejected with a 409 if the run isn't APPROVED, or a 400 if it has no payslips. Requires the six statutory/payable GL account ids as body fields (otherDeductionsPayableGlId is only required if the run actually has other-deduction amounts to post). Advances the run to POSTED and records the created journal entry's own id on the run.

get.summary: Get an employee profile
get.description: Includes department, salary structure, manager/direct-reports (id/name/jobTitle only), documents, next of kin, emergency contacts, asset assignments, onboarding tasks, and the exit record (with its own clearance items) if one exists.

patch.description: Rejects setting reportsToId to the employee's own id (an employee cannot report to themselves).

post.summary: Confirm an employee out of probation
post.description: Only valid while the employee is currently PROBATION — a discrete, auditable event, not implied by any other update.

post.summary: Log a transfer / promotion / demotion / secondment / contract-renewal event
post.description: Applies the event's own "to" values (department/job title/grade level) onto the Employee record in the same transaction as logging it, so the employment-history list is always an accurate record of what actually changed, not just a separately-tracked intent. A CONFIRMATION event type also flips employmentStatus to CONFIRMED and sets confirmationDate as a side effect — the same state POST :id/confirm above sets directly.

get.summary: List an employee's own employment-event history, most recent first
Get an entity's flat org-chart edge list
get.description: Active employees only (id/name/jobTitle/departmentId/reportsToId) — the caller reconstructs the tree from these edges; nothing pre-nested is returned.

post.summary: Attach a document to an employee
Record an employee's next of kin
Record an employee's emergency contact
Seed the standard onboarding checklist for a newly hired employee
post.description: Creates a fixed 7-item checklist (signed offer letter, IT provisioning, ID card, policy briefing, onboarding buddy, payroll & bank details, statutory registrations) with an optional shared due date. Rejected if the employee already has any onboarding task — this can only seed the checklist once.

post.summary: Add one extra onboarding task outside the standard checklist
Mark an onboarding task complete

get.summary: List an employee's onboarding tasks, ordered by due date

post.summary: Assign a company asset to an employee
Record a company asset as returned
post.description: Only valid while the assignment is currently ASSIGNED — an already-returned assignment is rejected.

get.summary: List every asset ever assigned to an employee, assigned and returned alike

post.summary: Raise a disciplinary case against an employee
Close a disciplinary case with an outcome
post.description: Rejected if the case is already CLOSED.

get.summary: List an employee's disciplinary cases, most recently raised first

post.summary: Initiate an employee exit
post.description: One exit record per employee — rejected if the employee already has one. clearanceChecklist maps department names to their own checklist item names (e.g. { IT: ["Return laptop"] }), and at least one item across all departments is required. In the same transaction, flips the employee's own employmentStatus to TERMINATED (exitType TERMINATION) or RESIGNED (every other exitType).

post.summary: Clear one item on an employee exit's own clearance checklist
post.description: A special-cased guard: an IT-department item whose own text mentions "asset" (a plain case-insensitive substring match on the item name, not a structured flag) cannot be cleared while the employee still has any ASSIGNED asset outstanding. Automatically rolls the parent exit record's own overall clearanceStatus up to COMPLETED once every item on the checklist is CLEARED — that rollup is not a separate call.

get.summary: Get an employee's exit record and its own clearance items

post.summary: Create a leave type
post.description: code is unique per entity (409 if it already exists). isPaid defaults true, carryForwardAllowed defaults false, and maxCarryForwardDays defaults 0 when omitted.

get.summary: List leave types
get.description: entityId is an optional filter; omit it to list every leave type across every entity.

post.summary: Initialize (or reset) an employee's leave balance for a type/year
post.description: 404s if the leave type does not exist. An upsert: calling this again for the same employee/type/year resets entitledDays back to the leave type's current daysPerYear and overwrites carriedForwardDays, but leaves usedDays completely untouched either way — re-initializing does not zero out leave already taken.

get.summary: List an employee's leave balances
get.description: year is an optional filter; omit it to see balances across every year on record.

post.summary: Request leave
post.description: Rejected (400) if endDate is before startDate, or if the requested day count exceeds the employee's available balance (entitledDays + carriedForwardDays - usedDays) for that leave type/year — a missing balance record is treated as 0 available, not unlimited. Starts SUBMITTED. Needs only hr.view — this is a self-service action.

get.summary: List leave requests
get.description: employeeId and status are both optional filters.

post.summary: Approve a submitted leave request
post.description: Only valid from SUBMITTED. Re-checks the balance again at approval time, independently of the check requestLeave already made — a 409 here means the balance was consumed by another approval in the meantime, a real race the service defends against rather than trusting the original request-time check alone. On success, in one transaction: increments usedDays on the balance AND upserts an ON_LEAVE attendance record for every day in the requested range.

post.summary: Reject a submitted leave request
post.description: Only valid from SUBMITTED. No balance or attendance changes — those only happen on approval.

post.summary: Cancel a leave request
post.description: Only valid from DRAFT or SUBMITTED — an already-APPROVED request cannot be cancelled through this route. Needs only hr.view — this is a self-service action.

post.summary: Add a public holiday
post.description: No uniqueness check — adding the same date and entity twice creates two rows, not a 409.

get.summary: List public holidays for an entity
get.description: entityId is required; year is an optional filter narrowing to that calendar year (Jan 1 to Dec 31 UTC).

get.summary: Get approved leave for an entity within a date range
get.description: entityId, from, and to are all required. Only APPROVED requests are included — SUBMITTED/REJECTED/CANCELLED ones never appear here regardless of date. Matches any request whose own date range overlaps [from, to] at all, not just requests that start within it.

post.summary: Create a shift
post.description: code is unique per entity (409 if it already exists). breakMinutes defaults to 0 when omitted.

get.summary: List shifts
get.description: entityId is an optional filter; omit it to list every shift across every entity.

post.summary: Assign an employee to a shift for one date
post.description: An upsert on (employeeId, date) — re-assigning the same employee on a date they already have an assignment for silently overwrites the shift, it does not 409.

get.summary: List shift assignments for a date range
get.description: entityId, from, and to are all required — unlike most list routes in this controller, none of the three is optional here.

post.summary: Clock in
post.description: An upsert on (employeeId, date) — a second clock-in the same day overwrites the first rather than 409ing. Status is computed automatically: LATE if a shift is assigned for the day and the clock-in is more than 15 minutes past the shift start time, PRESENT otherwise. Needs only hr.view, not hr.manage — this is a self-service action, not an admin one.

post.summary: Clock out
post.description: 404s if there is no clock-in record for this employee already today — clock-out cannot create a record on its own. Same hr.view self-service level as clock-in.

get.summary: List one employee's attendance records
get.description: from and to are both optional — omitting either leaves that end of the date range unbounded.

post.summary: Mark every active employee with no attendance record for a day as ABSENT
post.description: Meant to run as an end-of-day batch job. Only creates records for employees with no record at all that day — never touches or overwrites an existing record, including one already marked ABSENT.

post.summary: Register a biometric device
post.description: deviceIdentifier is unique per entity (409 if already registered). No vendor SDK is wired in here — any hardware vendor integrates by having its own adapter call pushBiometricEvent with whatever raw employee code the device reports.

get.summary: List biometric devices
get.description: entityId is an optional filter; omit it to list every device across every entity.

post.summary: Ingest a raw punch event from a biometric device
post.description: 404s if the device is unknown, 400s if it is registered but inactive. Stores the event unprocessed — matching it to an actual employee and folding it into an AttendanceRecord happens separately, via reconcile.

post.summary: Fold unprocessed biometric punches into attendance records
post.description: Matches events to Employee.employeeCode; a code that matches no employee is left unprocessed for manual review rather than silently dropped. For each matched employee/day, takes the earliest CLOCK_IN and latest CLOCK_OUT among that day's events (not every individual punch) and upserts one AttendanceRecord, computing LATE/PRESENT the same way clock-in does.

post.summary: Create a performance cycle
post.description: Starts OPEN. The (entityId, name) pair must be unique — reusing a name for the same entity is rejected rather than creating a second cycle with the same label.

get.summary: List performance cycles
get.description: Optionally filtered to one entityId, newest start date first.

post.summary: Move a cycle into calibration
post.description: Only an OPEN cycle can start calibration. From here, reviews in this cycle are expected to move through peer feedback and calibration rather than further self/manager edits.

post.summary: Close a performance cycle
post.description: Only a CALIBRATION cycle can be closed, and only once every review in it has reached COMPLETED — closing with any review still short of that is rejected, naming how many are outstanding.

post.summary: Create a goal (OKR) for an employee
post.description: Starts NOT_STARTED. cycleId is optional — a goal can exist outside any specific performance cycle.

post.summary: Update a goal's progress
post.description: progressPercent must be 0-100. Status is derived automatically from the value, not set directly: 0 stays NOT_STARTED, 1-99 becomes IN_PROGRESS, 100 becomes COMPLETED.

get.summary: List an employee's goals
get.description: Optionally filtered to one cycleId.

post.summary: Create a KPI for an employee
post.description: weight defaults to 0 when omitted.

post.summary: Record a KPI's actual value
post.description: Overwrites actualValue directly — no history of prior values is kept.

get.summary: List an employee's KPIs
get.description: Optionally filtered to one cycleId.

post.summary: Create a competency catalog entry
post.description: A shared, entity-wide competency (e.g. "Communication") that any employee can later be assessed against — not itself tied to one employee.

get.summary: List the competency catalog
get.description: Every competency on record, unfiltered.

post.summary: Assess an employee against a competency
post.description: rating must be between 1 and 5. cycleId is optional — an assessment can be recorded outside any specific performance cycle.

get.summary: List an employee's competency assessments
get.description: Each includes its own competency record. Optionally filtered to one cycleId.

post.summary: Submit a self-assessment
post.description: selfRating must be between 1 and 5. Upserts by (employeeId, cycleId) — resubmitting for the same employee/cycle updates the existing review rather than creating a second one. Creating one for the first time auto-assigns the reviewer as the employee's own manager (reportsToId) — an employee with no manager set cannot submit one.

post.summary: Submit the manager review for an existing review
post.description: managerRating must be between 1 and 5. The review must already exist (created via the self-assessment route) — this only updates it, it does not create one.

post.summary: Add peer feedback to a review
post.description: Appends to any existing peer comments (separated by "---") rather than overwriting them — this route can be called more than once per review, each call adding another peer's comments.

post.summary: Set the calibrated rating for a review
post.description: calibratedRating must be between 1 and 5, and the manager review must already be submitted — calibrating before that is rejected. The calibrated rating is the final agreed rating and may differ from the raw manager rating.

post.summary: Mark a review COMPLETED
post.description: The review must already have a calibrated rating — completing one before calibration is rejected.

get.summary: List reviews
get.description: Optionally filtered to one employeeId and/or one cycleId, newest first.

get.summary: Get an employee's completed review history
